title: LSD
description: LSD, the lsd visual look, is an optical state: light trails, slight double edges, oversaturated practicals, walls on a slow inhale. Perception is the set, not a scene of drug use and not a rainbow LUT.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Altered nights, music, a breakdown: one street or one room that will not stay put, a readable human so it remains a shot. Architecture breathes.
Lamps trail. Acid is the burned-print cousin.
This one is still wet. It is the wrong tool in a courtroom, a procedural, or any beat that needs carpenter-straight walls.
If the lamps do not trail and the room is still, you shot neon-noir.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is LSD in film?
An optical recipe: trails, breathing walls, too much chroma, a room that will not stay put. It is perception as set, not a scene of use.
LSD vs Acid
LSD is wet, trailing, architectural inhale. Acid is a print left in the sun: burned chroma, melting edges. Pick one. Trails belong to LSD. Damage belongs to acid.
When should I use LSD?
Altered nights, music, breakdowns. Skip courtrooms and any coverage that needs stable walls.
How do I prompt LSD for AI image or video?
